title.narrative: Greater Colombo Water and Wastewater Management Improvement Investment Program - Tranche 2

description.narrative:
On 25 October 2012, Asian Development Bank (ADB) approved a multitranche financing facility (MFF) of $300 million, envisaged to be funded from ADB's Ordinary Capital Resources (OCR) and Asian Development Fund (ADF), for the Greater Colombo Water and Wastewater Management Improvement Investment Program (the Investment Program). Tranche 1 ($84 million) under the Investment Program was approved by the President on 22 November 2012. The MFF is envisaged to comprise three additional tranches as follows: $88 million (Project 2 in 2013); $90 million (Project 3 in 2015); and $38 million (Project 4 in 2016). Tranches 1 and 2 focus on reducing non-revenue water (NRW) and improving water service efficiency in Greater Colombo. Tranches 3 and 4 will support improvement of wastewater collection and treatment facilities and management services in Greater Colombo. The Framework Financing Agreement (FFA) for the Investment Program was signed on 12 September 2012.
The Government submitted to ADB a periodic financing request (PFR) for Project 2, on 3 June 2013 (Appendix 1). The proposed Project 2 will continue investments in water supply, NRW reduction in the south part of Colombo city, and water supply service improvements for National Water Supply and Drainage Board (NWSDB). The proposed Project 2 will also support the Colombo Municipal Council (CMC) to complete the project preparation activities for the wastewater investments under Projects 3 and 4. The proposed Project 2 will include: (i) $80 million ADB loan from both OCR and ADF for investments in water supply improvements and NRW reduction; and (ii) $8 million ADB loan from ADF support for the CMC for advance action on wastewater investments. The ADB's Country Operations Business Plan, 2013-2015, for Sri Lanka includes a firm provision for Project 2 in 2013.

description.narrative: Improved system, efficiency and financial sustainability of water supply and wastewater services in Greater Colombo

By end 2018:
NRW in south part of Colombo city reduced to 20% (baseline: 49% in 2013) Achievement: 18 Progress/Status: 53 DMAs established, completed and handed over, and NRW reduced to 18%. Target overachieved. Project closed. L3029 financially closed on 17 July 2025. Data Source: NWSDB water balance audit

33,000 households benefitted with 24*7 water supply in towns east of Colombo (baseline water supply 5-6 hours in CBO areas in 2013) Achievement: 24 Progress/Status: 146,601 Connection transfers were completed. Target achieved. Project Closed. Data Source: NWSDB annual reports

44,500households (incl. all BPL and FHH households) benefitted with 24*7 water supply in the south part of Colombo city (baseline 5 hours in 2013) Achievement: 24 Progress/Status: Out of 41,428 established connections, 26,450 Connection transfers were completed. 24 hours service for 7 days per week achieved. Project Closed. Final loan L3029 financially will be closed on July 2025. Data Source: NWSDB annual reports

25% energy saving and cost reductions in water production through Ambathale pumping station refurbishments (baseline: annual energy costs $7.05 million in 2013) Achievement: To be assessed Progress/Status: AFD is financing $70 million for the Ambatale water supply system improvement and energy-saving project. ADB is responsible for procurement and safeguards monitoring. The November 2021 review mission had a meeting with the project director and the consultancy team. There are 3 civil contract packages under the AFD component. Contract for supplying and laying of 9km, 1200mm diameter DI pipes from Ambatale to Colombo city limits was awarded to JITF - KDESH JV ($16.50 million) in July 2016. The contract was scheduled to be completed in May 2018. This contractor was demobilized from the site in 2018 and has remobilized in the last quarter of 2019. The physical progress of this contract is 78% against the revised planned progress of 90%. The revised target date of completion is 31 May 2022. Contract for supply and laying of 5km, 1200mm diameter DI pipes from Gothatuwa to Colombo city limits and ground reservoir in Gothatuwa was awarded to CMEC-BPPE JV ($16.8 million) in August 2020. The physical progress of this contract is 52% against the target progress of 82%. The target date of completion is 31 May 2022. The contract for the replacement and rehabilitation of pumps at the Ambatale water treatment plant was awarded to Zhongnan-SZS-JH JV ($32 million) in the third quarter of 2018. The physical progress is 43% against the planned 100%. Loan extension and restructuring are still pending. AFD expects the implementation agency, National Water Supply and Drainage Board will complete all construction works before end of this year, using government funds. Data Source: NWSDB annual reports Actual value: To be assessed
